_config!A1: FRED Credit-Risk Dashboard -- CONFIG (the knob panel). Edit values here; no code change needed.
_config!C5: Optional: paste your FRED key here if you don't set the FRED_API_KEY environment variable. Get one free at https://fredaccount.stlouisfed.org/apikeys
_config!C6: auto|xlwings|openpyxl. xlwings writes into the open book.
_config!C7: TRUE = offline synthetic data (no key/network), for trying the button.
_config!C9: flag a series stale if older than this x its cadence.
_config!C10: Case-Shiller reports a month ~2 months after it ends (observed 95 days). Limit becomes 122.
_config!C11: Same Case-Shiller release cadence (observed 95 days). Limit becomes 122.
_config!C12: Fed G.19 consumer credit lands ~5 weeks after month end (observed 95 days). Limit becomes 122.
_config!C13: Fed household debt-service ratios land ~2.5 months after quarter end (observed 246 days). Limit becomes 259.
_config!C14: Z.1 Financial Accounts land ~2.5 months after quarter end (observed 246 days). Limit becomes 259.
_config!C15: seconds between FRED requests (FRED allows ~120/min; keep >=0.5).
_config!C16: retries with backoff if FRED returns a rate-limit error.
_config!C17: OPTIONAL YYYY-MM-DD: pin FRED realtime to reproduce a past vintage (audit trail). Blank = latest release (default).
_config!C21: flag a loss/delinquency series when its 8-period z-score >= this.
_config!D21: UNCALIBRATED DEFAULT (1 sigma) -- not fitted to a KeyBank loss series. Set and cite a basis (owner/date/backtest) before production use.
_config!C22: flag a SLOOS series when net-tightening >= this (percent).
_config!D22: UNCALIBRATED DEFAULT (20 net %) -- illustrative, not calibrated. Set and cite a basis (owner/date/rationale) before production use.

_readme!A5: A self-contained, reusable template. One workbook pulls credit-risk data from
_readme!A6: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data), lands it raw, and presents it as
_readme!A7: formula-driven dashboards plus a geographic stress watchlist for commercial
_readme!A8: loan-portfolio targeting. All code, config and docs live inside this workbook,
_readme!A9: so it can be emailed, opened on another machine, and re-run with one click.
_readme!A12: 1. Install Python 3 (add it to PATH) and the dependencies:
_readme!A13: pip install fredapi xlwings openpyxl pandas
_readme!A14: 2. Get a free FRED API key: https://fredaccount.stlouisfed.org/apikeys
_readme!A15: 3. Provide the key ONE of two ways (never hardcoded in code):
_readme!A16: - set an environment variable  FRED_API_KEY=your_key   (preferred), or
_readme!A17: - paste it into the _config tab: [SETTINGS] -> fred_api_key cell.
_readme!A18: 4. Enable macros when prompted (the button needs them).
_readme!A20: RUN IT  (the workbook is already the finished product; you only add data)
_readme!A21: 1. In Excel press Alt+F8 -> run ExtractFiles. It writes three files next to the
_readme!A22: workbook: runner.py (from the _code_py tab), requirements.txt, and RUN.txt
_readme!A23: (the exact PowerShell commands). Nothing runs inside Excel.
_readme!A25: 3. Open RUN.txt and follow it from PowerShell: install the deps, then run
_readme!A26: runner.py --backend openpyxl against the closed workbook. It pulls FRED per
_readme!A27: _config and writes the data into the file.
_readme!A28: 4. Reopen the workbook -- the formulas recalc into the populated dashboards.
_readme!A29: No key yet? Set _config demo_mode = TRUE before step 1 and use the --demo
_readme!A30: command in RUN.txt (offline synthetic data). For live data, set the
_readme!A31: FRED_API_KEY environment variable or the _config cell. Optional: after
_readme!A32: reopening, Alt+F8 -> PaintSparklines draws the Trend column (native sparklines
_readme!A33: are the one thing the data step can't write).
_readme!A36: Every tab is styled from keybank_style.py (tokens + helpers) -- so this
_readme!A37: workbook and any future one built from the template look like one family.
_readme!A38: Black grounds, red leads sparingly, neutrals breathe. Dashboards: black banner
_readme!A39: + red rule, KPI tiles, brand-muted heat on the z-score column, and an optional
_readme!A40: 8-quarter sparkline per row. Watchlist: the red geographic-boundary gate.
_readme!A45: prior, YoY, an 8-period z-score, a Flag column, and an (optional) trend
_readme!A47: Watchlist_Geo  -- states & metros ranked by house-price deterioration (YoY).
_readme!A49: _config  -- THE KNOB PANEL: series dictionary, threshold bands, key fallback.
_readme!A50: _code_py / _code_vba  -- the runner and macro as plain text.
